en: Avoid touching the sap of the Philippine Dita tree, as its bitter latex compounds can cause severe skin and eye irritation in humans.
Female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes spread the dengue virus, so removing stagnant water around your house prevents them from laying eggs.
Brushing your teeth twice daily removes plaque, a sticky film of bacteria that produces acids which destroy tooth enamel.
If a stray dog bites you, wash the wound with soap and running water for fifteen minutes to reduce rabies risk.
Eating raw or undercooked red kidney beans causes severe vomiting because they contain a natural toxin called phytohaemagglutinin.
Drinking untreated water from rivers can expose you to Giardia, a microscopic parasite that causes severe stomach cramps and diarrhea.
Inhaling spores from black mold growing on damp walls can trigger asthma attacks and severe allergic reactions in sensitive children.
Applying sunscreen with SPF 30 blocks about ninety-seven percent of the sun's ultraviolet B rays, preventing painful sunburns and skin damage.
Removing a bee stinger by scraping it sideways with a card prevents the venom sac from pumping more poison into your skin.
Washing your hands with soap for twenty seconds physically removes and destroys the lipid envelope of influenza viruses, stopping you from catching colds.
Pulling a tick straight out with tweezers prevents its mouthparts from breaking off and leaving infection-causing bacteria inside your skin.
Wearing flip-flops in public showers prevents athlete's foot, a contagious fungal infection that thrives in moist environments and causes itchy peeling skin.
